query: Which method can be used for concurrent strength–ductility improvement, and why?

generation.hypothesis: If an aluminum alloy is subjected to accumulative roll bonding followed by a moderate annealing step, then the resulting refined, partially recrystallized microstructure will exhibit both higher strength and retained ductility compared to the unprocessed (as-cast or as-rolled) state.
generation.material_initial_state: Aluminum alloy in the as-cast or solution-treated condition
generation.intervention: Applying multiple passes of accumulative roll bonding, then performing a short annealing heat treatment at an intermediate temperature
generation.conditions: Uniform rolling reductions, controlled heating rate, and moderate annealing times that promote partial recrystallization but limit excessive grain growth
generation.structural_mediator: Ultrafine-grained regions and clean grain boundaries formed via severe plastic deformation followed by partial recrystallization
generation.mechanism: Balancing dislocation-based strengthening with minimized grain growth, preserving both elevated yield strength and unexpectedly high elongation
generation.predicted_outcome: Concurrent improvement in tensile strength (by a moderate factor, e.g. around 50% or more) and ductility compared to baseline
generation.baseline: Mechanical performance of the same alloy in its unprocessed or as-cast form
generation.boundary: Excessively high annealing temperatures or prolonged times can lead to grain coarsening that negates the advantage of refined structures
generation.uncertainty: Optimum rolling pass reduction and annealing conditions are not completely established, so fine-tuning is required to maximize combined strength and ductility

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare identical aluminum alloy blanks, apply accumulative roll bonding with varying total strains, anneal at different temperatures for set durations, then measure the mechanical properties and microstructures for each condition.
measurements: Tensile properties (yield strength, ultimate tensile strength, elongation)
Dislocation density (X-ray diffraction or transmission electron microscopy)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If any processed condition fails to exhibit simultaneous improvements in strength and ductility relative to the baseline, the hypothesis that this combined method enhances both properties is invalid.
